Name: Marine Engine Fault
Summary: Test-bench time series from a marine diesel engine with a baseline run and five physically induced fault classes at several loads, labelled row by row.
Description:
Marine Engine Fault records a marine diesel engine on a test bench for research on condition monitoring, fault diagnosis and anomaly detection. The engine is a Matsui Iron Works MU323DGSC. Ahmad BahooToroody of Aalto University and co-authors from the University of Turku and Politecnico di Milano published it on Zenodo in 2026 under CC BY 4.0, alongside a data descriptor submitted to Scientific Data.

Besides a baseline recording, five faults were physically induced on the engine: compressor air-filter clogging, air-cooler fouling, injection-valve nozzle clogging, cooling-water pump cavitation and turbine degradation, each at one or more loads between 40 and 85 %.

The 16 CSV files hold roughly 115,000 time-stamped samples over about 70 channels, such as engine speed, in-cylinder pressures, exhaust and cooling temperatures, flows and efficiency values. Fault files carry a binary pre-anomaly or anomaly label on every row; the reference file has none. A file index, a variable dictionary and the normalisation script are included.
